doc.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Sixties: Verve end, California, Half Note, Duets
title: Marriage to Tavia and the Upper West Side neighborhood
summary: They recall his second wife, the cats and dog, and neighbors Paul Motian and Elvin Jones.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: By the way when did you meet Tavia? His second wife for those of you watching this who don’t know who Tavia was.
It was in the beginning of the sixties I believe.
When I met you the two of you were living at one hundred and seventh and Central Park West.
I remember taking the train over there for lessons for a couple years. It was the two of you and Hugo and Luigi, the cats?
Who were on the cover of the Spirits album with your upright piano that you had then in your apartment.
Then we added this nice dog and the cats used to sit and swipe him when he walked by.
That neighborhood. Wasn’t Paul Motian and Barry Altschul were in that neighborhood right?
Paul Motian lived upstairs as he still does.
Barry Altschul was a couple blocks away I think.
I don’t remember that. I think Elvin Jones was a block or two away and Max. Maybe they lived in the same building or something.
